title: In how many ways can A be joined to make a straight angle?
description: Two dot grids each show the points A and B joined by a line. A is joined to another dot so that the two lines make a straight angle, and the dots on the line through A and B, on the far side of A, are counted in each grid. A ruler laid along the line is the check.
teaching_notes: One idea: a straight angle needs the new arm on the same line as AB, on the other side of A. Watch for students who join A to dots that are off the line.

video_script.why: The child finds all the dots that make a straight angle with a given line by staying on the same line, on the other side of the vertex.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two dot grids, each with A and B joined
video_script.anchor: two dot grids, seven columns by six rows, each with A and B joined
video_script.payoff_line: The left grid has three ways, and the right grid has two ways

final_answer.value: left grid 3 ways, right grid 2 ways; the new segment must lie on the same line as AB, on the opposite side of A
final_answer.spoken: the left grid has three ways, and the right grid has two ways, because the new line must lie on the line of eigh bee, on the other side of eigh

maths_rules: two grids of 7 columns by 6 rows; a straight angle needs the new arm on the same line as AB, on the opposite side of A
left grid: A at row 3, column 4 and B at row 3, column 7; AB goes right, so the new arm goes left to the dots in columns 1, 2 and 3 of row 3: 3 ways

right grid: A at row 3, column 3 and B at row 5, column 5; AB goes down and right through the dot at row 4, column 4, so the new arm goes up and left to the dots at row 2, column 2 and row 1, column 1: 2 ways
check: a ruler along AB, slid past A, touches exactly these dots
video_script.design: One idea: stay on the line of AB and go to the other side of A. The two grids stay on the board.
open_questions: The positions of A and B in the two grids follow the worklist's description of the book's figures; the figures could not be viewed, so the counts three and two are not checked against the pictures.
